result.name: Unified Digital Marketplace Interface
result.business_requirement: The business requires a unified digital interface that aggregates fragmented inventory from multiple store partners to present a comprehensive assortment to customers.
result.business_objective: This serves the goal of simplifying the shopping experience and enabling monetization through transaction commissions and advertising on a consolidated marketplace.
result.business_value: Meeting this requirement increases customer retention and revenue; failure results in a fragmented user experience and lost sales opportunities.
success_measures: proposed 95% of customers find all required items in a single search
proposed 20% increase in average order value due to cross-store availability
proposed reduction in customer support queries regarding stock availability by 30%
policies_and_constraints: Inventory data must be synchronized in real-time to prevent overselling.
The interface must comply with data privacy regulations regarding customer location and purchase history.
Store partners must retain the right to define their own product categorization within the unified catalog.
assumptions: Store partners will provide accurate and up-to-date inventory feeds via API.
Customers expect a seamless browsing experience without distinguishing between different store sources.
Network latency will not exceed thresholds that delay inventory updates during peak hours.
risks_and_dependencies: Dependency on the Order Allocation Engine to validate inventory availability before display.
Risk of data inconsistency if store partners fail to update stock levels promptly.
Potential complexity in managing conflicting pricing or promotional offers across different store partners.

fr_relationships.reason: FR-054 enables the 'Order Request' object creation, which is the primary user action within the 'Unified Digital Marketplace Interface' described in BR-002. It directly supports the objective of presenting a comprehensive assortment for selection.

FR-062 focuses on aggregating feedback for strategic insights. While this supports the 'business value' of retention and improvement mentioned in BR-002, it does not directly support the core functional requirement of the BR, which is the *presentation* and *aggregation of inventory* for immediate shopping. It is a downstream benefit rather than a direct enabler of the marketplace interface functionality.

findings.finding: FR-062 (Feedback Aggregation) is weakly linked to the core definition of the BR (Unified Digital Marketplace Interface). The BR focuses on inventory aggregation and presentation, whereas FR-062 focuses on post-transaction data analysis.
findings.evidence: BR-002 text: 'aggregates fragmented inventory... to present a comprehensive assortment'. FR-062 text: 'aggregate feedback records to generate actionable insights'.
findings.recommendation: Review if FR-062 is truly essential for the 'Unified Digital Marketplace Interface' or if it belongs to a separate 'Analytics & Strategy' BR. Consider adding an FR specifically for 'Unified Catalog Aggregation' or 'Real-time Inventory Synchronization' to better support the BR.

findings.finding: The assumption regarding network latency is technically specific and lacks a defined threshold, making it difficult to validate against business constraints.
findings.evidence: Assumption: 'Network latency will not exceed thresholds that delay inventory updates during peak hours.'
findings.recommendation: Define specific latency thresholds (e.g., <200ms) or reference an external SLA document to make this assumption testable.

semantic.assessment_summary: The Business Requirement (BR-002) is well-defined with clear business value, meaningful objectives, and appropriate success measures. It avoids solution leakage by focusing on the 'what' (unified interface) rather than the 'how'. However, the linkage to Functional Requirement FR-062 is weak; FR-062 addresses post-transaction analytics rather than the core inventory aggregation and presentation function of the BR. A dedicated FR for catalog/inventory aggregation would strengthen the requirement set.
